reply: Let's use the full option, to evaluate the performance of the kev option and compare it with the already trusted laya option. We want to develop the intuition and tools to create deciders for different use cases over time, and the motivation classifier is the second example after the antisemite posts classifiers. We can run the classifier in a batch mode, which can make the inference cost-effective even with the larger memory requirement, and even the GPU options that we saw can speed things up compared to the CPU option.
option_scope: full: 100 eval + all 295 train rows (395 rows), bias and temperature fitted on train rows only; projected 18.8 h CPU and peak RSS about 40 GB (2.4 x the GGUF bytes, 12.97 GB measured on one row)
